Q2: 'The Great Siege'. The caption '1779 — The Great Siege' appears at frame 23 (21 Jun 1779). Camps of many tiny soldiers or tents then grow on the land beside the Rock, and ships gather in the bay. So a long siege of the Rock by a land and sea force begins.
Q3: Not sure. The pictures never show food, empty stores or starving people. The siege seems to cut the town off: enemy camps on land and ships blockading the bay. People in the town are only hinted at as short of supplies (small figures on the slope and in the streets), so I can't say for certain.
Q4: A fleet of many ships sails in from the sea. It appears around 18 Jan 1780 (frame 47) and again on 12 Apr 1781 (frames 53-56), arriving at the town's harbour and walls. I read these as relief or supply ships, but nothing on screen says so.
